deities: Adi Subrahmanya (Subrahmanya worshipped in an anthill/Putta)
festivals: Annual Rathotsava of the main Kukke temple (Karthika-Margashira)

history.period: Unknown - subsidiary shrine of the Kukke Subrahmanya complex
history.summary: SUB-SHRINE WITHIN THE KUKKE COMPLEX (SEQ 1688): the Adi Subrahmanya temple lies north-east of the main Kukke Sri Subrahmanya Temple, ~1.2 km away; a visit here is traditionally considered necessary to complete the Kukke pilgrimage. Here Lord Subrahmanya is worshipped in an anthill (Putta), said to have medicinal properties; offerings of mirrors and Naga images are made. The Sarpa Samskara pooja hall stands close to this shrine. No independent founding date is published (unverified). RELATED RECORD of seq 1688, not an exact duplicate. Image shows the Kukke Subrahmanya complex; no dedicated verified image of the anthill shrine was found.

name: Adi Subrahmanya Temple
town_description: Subramanya (Kukke Subramanya) is a pilgrimage village in Sullia/Kadaba taluk of Dakshina Kannada district, Karnataka, on the banks of the Kumaradhara river. Set in the forested Western Ghats at the foot of Kumara Parvatha, it is renowned for the Kukke Sri Subrahmanya Temple, the foremost centre of Naga worship and Sarpa Samskara rituals in South India. It is also the base for the popular Kumara Parvatha trek.

travel.road: Well connected by road from Mangalore (~105 km) and Bangalore (~270 km); frequent KSRTC buses; Dharmasthala ~54 km away
